Context: Hu Yaobang served as an official in China under Deng Xiaoping and Premier Li Peng.
Title: Document 5
Subtitle: Chinese Students Begin Protests at Tiananmen Square, 1989
Content: `text(Six days)` after the death of Hu Yaobang, the deposed reform-minded leader of the Chinese Communist Party, some `text(100,000)` students gathered at Beijing's Tiananmen Square to commemorate Hu and voice their discontent with China's authoritative communist government. The `text(next day)`, an official memorial service for Hu Yaobang was held in Tiananmen's Great Hall of the People, and student representatives carried a petition to the steps of the Great Hall, demanding to meet with Premier Li Peng. The Chinese government refused such a meeting, leading to a general boycott of Chinese universities across the country and widespread calls for democratic reforms.

Ignoring government warnings of violent suppression of any mass demonstration, students from more than `40` universities began a march to Tiananmen on `text(April 27)`. The students were joined by workers, intellectuals, and civil servants, and by `text(mid-May)` more than a `text(million)` people filled the square, the site of communist leader's Mao Zedong's proclamation of the People's Republic of China in `1949`. On `text(May 20)`, the government formally declared martial law in Beijing, and troops and tanks were called in to disperse the dissidents. However, large numbers of students and citizens blocked the army's advance, and by `text(May 23)` government forces had pulled back to the outskirts of Beijing...
